symptom: A turn or tool call without threadId can query and consume pending background results for the target agent across all conversations and resources.
expected: Pending results must be selected and consumed only inside an explicit resource/conversation/thread scope; missing scope must be rejected.
actual: PendingUpdatesProcessor falls back to all unconsumed background_task/automation_job records for the agent and marks returned IDs consumed. checkPendingUpdates also treats threadId as optional and otherwise scopes only by target agent.
rootCause: The no-thread fallback omits resource/conversation predicates before read and consume operations.
impactOnTargetArchitecture: Cross-conversation/cross-user disclosure and misdelivery path; a durable inbox/outbox must fail closed on missing routing identity.

symptom: A direct metaAgent.generate call that supplies a thread but omits resource uses the constant resource meta-agent while Meta working memory is resource-scoped by default.
expected: A user-facing memory-enabled agent must reject missing resource identity or derive a user-specific resource, never an agent-global resource.
actual: The Meta wrapper passes memory.resourceId ?? META_AGENT_ID; the harness uses it as memory resource. Meta enables working memory without an explicit scope, whose installed default is resource scope.
rootCause: A process-wide agent ID is used as fallback resource identity on a resource-scoped working-memory path.
impactOnTargetArchitecture: Calls omitting resource identity can share user preferences and project scratchpad across unrelated conversations/users.

symptom: One persisted thread accepted messages from two different resources instead of rejecting the resource mismatch.
expected: A thread has one immutable resource owner; a call using the same threadId with another resourceId must fail before writing any message.
actual: The resource-b generate on thread-a completed. mastra_threads retained thread-a owner resource-a, while mastra_messages contained thread-a messages attributed to both resource-a and resource-b.
suspectedLayer: Mastra memory thread ownership enforcement and message persistence
rootCause: The effective generate/storage path did not enforce immutable thread ownership before message persistence; the exact internal layer is not yet isolated.
impactOnTargetArchitecture: A cross-resource caller can append to another resource's conversation and contaminate context, a direct user-isolation violation.

symptom: Prose, malformed JSON, invalid status, and empty input normalize to status ok; empty delegation result strings bypass wrapper validation.
expected: Missing, empty, malformed, or invalid result contracts must remain non-success until validated or repaired.
actual: The deterministic parser test observed prose, invalid status, malformed JSON, empty/undefined input, and non-envelope JSON falling back to ok/parsed=false. The wrapper downgrades only failed/blocked_needs_approval and skips empty result strings.
rootCause: The compatibility fallback encodes absence or invalidity of the machine-readable contract as success.
impactOnTargetArchitecture: False completion can suppress retry/approval and feed invalid inputs into review/synthesis.

symptom: The common tool envelope drops Mastra ToolExecutionContext, including abortSignal and request/runtime context, before calling the wrapped implementation.
expected: Tool wrappers must preserve the framework second execute argument so cancellation and request-scoped services reach underlying work.
actual: Mastra invokes execute(input, options), while withToolEnvelope returns a one-argument function and substitutes a custom metadata object.
rootCause: The wrapper public signature and inner execute contract were narrowed to one argument.
impactOnTargetArchitecture: Cancelled or timed-out runs cannot reliably stop wrapped long-running tools and lose request-level identity/runtime services.

symptom: A synchronous pipeline delegation timeout rejects only the caller wait; the underlying agent.generate receives no AbortSignal and can continue.
expected: Every delegation deadline must abort active generation and tools, then verify actual stop before terminalizing.
actual: Pipeline agents use bare agent.generate; delegate-task wraps the promise with a timeout Promise.race whose timeout branch only rejects.
rootCause: The lightweight pipeline wrapper has no abort/deadline input and its caller uses a wait-only timeout.
impactOnTargetArchitecture: Timed-out pipeline work can continue consuming premium models or producing late side effects after reported failure.

symptom: A pre-aborted direct generate was not rejected and persisted a user message.
expected: An already-aborted signal must fail before provider invocation and before any memory write.
actual: Three isolated repetitions completed in 18-19 ms instead of throwing, and each left the user input in persisted messages.
suspectedLayer: direct Agent.generate abort check versus memory write ordering
rootCause: The exact layer that ignores or observes the pre-aborted signal too late is unknown.
impactOnTargetArchitecture: Cancel cannot be trusted as a no-more-work/no-more-write boundary even before dispatch.

symptom: Async delegation persists a running record but executes the attempt as an unawaited promise in the request process; no recovery/claim worker for async_delegations is present.
expected: Accepted background work must be claimed from durable state, leased, recoverable after process death, and fenced against stale completion.
actual: startAsyncDelegation inserts running and immediately calls void executeDelegation. The Mastra instance does not enable native backgroundTasks and no production bootstrap resumes running async_delegations records.
rootCause: Persistence records metadata/result state, but execution ownership remains a process-local promise without durable dispatch, lease, checkpoint, or recovery.
impactOnTargetArchitecture: A crash can strand accepted work and suppress result delivery.

symptom: Two overlapping harness attempts with the same taskId and no runId collapsed into one runtime run identity and one run row.
expected: taskId identifies durable intent while every attempt receives a distinct immutable runId/attemptId and independent mutable state.
actual: Both calls returned the same runId equal to taskId. Mongo contained one agent_runs row, two started and two completed events, and two output artifacts under that one run identity.
suspectedLayer: run identity and in-memory harness state
rootCause: generateWithHarness derives runId as input.runId ?? input.taskId, while deadline, depth, and reflector registries are keyed solely by runId.
impactOnTargetArchitecture: Parallel/retry attempts overwrite correlation and mutable run state, so cleanup or late completion can act on the wrong attempt.

symptom: The harness deadline is enforced only around the first agent.generate; optional repair/review/deliberation/approval/completion passes can call the model without timeout or AbortSignal.
expected: One aggregate deadline and cancellation signal must cover precontext, primary generation, all postpasses, persistence, and terminalization.
actual: callAgentGenerate uses AbortController plus withTimeout for the primary call. Later no-tool gates and repair passes directly await agent.generate before run cleanup.
rootCause: Published deadline state is not consumed by post-generation model passes.
impactOnTargetArchitecture: Runs can exceed their declared deadline and remain impossible to stop during postprocessing.

symptom: Async completion queues a pending message but does not autonomously re-enter the front agent; delivery waits for another user turn or explicit polling.
expected: A terminal worker event should atomically enqueue one result and wake the owning conversation for review/synthesis/notification.
actual: The custom contract explicitly says pickup occurs on the next user interaction. The processor runs before a turn, and native background tasks/streamUntilIdle continuation are not enabled.
rootCause: Pending messages are a pull-on-next-turn queue, not an event-driven conversation inbox with wake/subscription.
impactOnTargetArchitecture: Fan-out review/synthesis cannot complete autonomously and notifications may remain pending indefinitely.

symptom: Meta root harness wraps generate only; stream and streamUntilIdle retain original Agent implementations.
expected: All public front channels must share identity, memory, budget, GoalContract, policy, result, and cleanup behavior.
actual: installMetaAgentHarness stores and replaces only agent.generate; there is no stream wrapper.
rootCause: The harness monkey-patches one method instead of using a channel-independent execution gateway.
impactOnTargetArchitecture: Behavior, telemetry, deadlines, and safety guarantees differ by client channel.

symptom: Pipeline agents use a lightweight reflection wrapper around bare agent.generate and bypass the full shared harness.
expected: Every execution profile must provide equivalent identity, aggregate budget, result validation, cancellation, evidence, and terminalization contracts.
actual: delegate-task explicitly selects a no-full-harness path; generatePipelineWithReflection supplies memory/prepareStep and calls agent.generate directly.
rootCause: Pipeline phase tooling was integrated as a parallel gateway rather than a profile inside the common harness.
impactOnTargetArchitecture: Pipeline jobs have distinct timeout/cancel/result/observability semantics.

symptom: Ten Agent Board targets completed isolated no-tool local-provider smoke calls with empty response text in two separate runs.
expected: A safe one-step deterministic prompt with toolChoice none returns non-empty domain text or an explicit error.
actual: Both board-smoke runs produced empty text and zero tools for the same ten agents. Provider/control calls returned non-empty text, so a general Ollama outage was not observed.
rootCause: Unknown; the repeated empty response is confirmed but was not isolated to prompt, model adapter, processor, or agent configuration.
impactOnTargetArchitecture: These agents cannot be classified as interactively usable on the tested local execution profile until the empty-output boundary is diagnosed.

symptom: The intended npx tsx path could not start temporary TypeScript tests.
expected: Baseline tests use only the repository's already installed local runner and never fetch dependencies.
actual: npx found no local tsx binary, attempted registry resolution, and failed with ENOTFOUND. No package was installed; later tests used the installed Mastra esbuild loader path.
rootCause: tsx is not locally installed and npx attempted a forbidden/unavailable network fetch.
impactOnTargetArchitecture: This is a baseline test-environment gap, not an application failure; reproducible isolated runners must be provisioned before future chaos suites.
